not_fixed.title: fabric/api.py build() allocates 5 of the 9 module-level names state_dict()'s docstring lists as checkpointed Parameters (halt_b, norm, q_entry, nov_proj are declared but never built)
not_fixed.detail: state_dict()'s own docstring already distinguishes this case from `ctrl` (which WAS dropped from the list): it explicitly rules that q_entry and nov_proj 'stay, because both walks use them', i.e. build() is meant to eventually allocate them, unlike ctrl which belongs only to the unported transition arm. So trimming the list (the way ctrl was trimmed) would contradict an already-recorded, dated resolution, and is not the right repair here. The alternative -- allocating the four modules now -- is only safely specified for `norm` (a LayerNorm over d_model, per forward's own docstring: 'head(norm(state)) per hop for the vote') and arguably `nov_proj` (a projection of the (B,) novelty scalar into the dk-dimensional route-query space, per 'NOVELTY ENTERS THE QUERY'). `q_entry` and `halt_b` have no specified shape anywhere in the reachable tree: the docstring's only evidence is two dangling old-tree line references (:2557, :2564, :2554) that this tree cannot resolve, docs/04_CONTRACT.md has zero mentions of either name (grepped), and forward()/state_dict() -- the only functions that would consume them -- are both still `raise NotImplementedError` stubs, so there is no code to check a guessed shape against. Allocating two well-specified modules and leaving two guessed would not close the finding (state_dict would still overclaim two names) and allocating all four on a guess risks baking a wrong geometry into a 'frozen' module dict that a later forward()/load_state_dict() implementer would have to detect and repair -- worse than the current, explicitly-latent state, since forward() itself cannot exercise any of these four modules yet regardless. Left build() unchanged; this needs an owner to specify q_entry's and halt_b's shapes (or state authoritatively that build() should wait for the same commit that writes forward()).

not_fixed.title: memory/api.py open_store's mem.key_depth Gate reports FIRED whenever MEM_KEY_SRC=model on the transformer arm, which the finding says is wrong because LM.encode structurally ignores its own n_layers parameter
not_fixed.detail: Verified against the CURRENT tree rather than trusting the filed evidence: lm/api.py::encode (lines ~552-561, current tree) now reads n_layers (`n_run = model.geom.layers if n_layers is None else int(n_layers)`) and loops `model.body.layers[:n_run]`, genuinely truncating the transformer stack -- the premise the finding rests on ('encode's body never references its own n_layers parameter... encode(cfg,m,x,n_layers=1) and encode(cfg,m,x) return byte-identical tensors') is now false. Reproduced directly: built a real LM (LM_ARCH=transformer, LM_LAYERS=4) and called encode() with and without n_layers=1 -- max|dh| = 5.28 (nonzero: the truncation has a real effect). Then reproduced the finding's own MEM-side repro: open_store(MEM_KEY_SRC=model, LM_ARCH=transformer, MEM_KEY_DEPTH=3) -> Gate(name='mem.key_depth', fired=True, value=3, threshold=0, reachable=True, reason=''). This is now CORRECT: the mechanism the Gate claims ran (a depth-cut encode) genuinely can and does run on this configuration, so FIRED is the right state per spine/gate.py's own three-state contract. This appears to have been fixed by whoever owns lm/api.py (not me, and not in this session) since round2's audit was filed; no code change made in memory/api.py for this item, since the code it was filed against is now correct.

not_fixed.title: ckpt/api.py save_period returns a bare units.Windows and declares no Gate for the dir-set/every==0 condition ('the only saves are the final one plus SIGUSR1'), though its own DID IT FIRE line claims one
not_fixed.detail: Confirmed still present: save_period's body is unchanged (`ckpt = ckpt.owned_by('CKPT'); return U.Windows(int(ckpt.every))`), spine.gate is not imported anywhere in ckpt/api.py, and no counters()/gates() accessor exists anywhere in the package (unlike FAB, which has a `counters` entry point already declared in its frozen surface, or FAB.build/MEM.open_store, which attach a `.gates` tuple to the stateful object they return). The blocker is architectural, not a missing few lines: (1) save_period's return value is read directly, unwrapped, into a periods dict at three call sites in spine/compose.py (`periods={'ckpt': ckpt_api.save_period(ck), ...}`), which I do not own -- changing its return shape breaks that. (2) CKPT has no persistent stateful object analogous to FAB's Population or MEM's Store that a Gate could ride on the way pop.gates/store.gates do -- CKPT's frozen surface, as written, declares no counters()/gates() entry point at all, unlike FAB and MEM. (3) Adding a brand-new public function (e.g. a `gates(ckpt)` or `counters(ckpt)`) would itself change the tree's entry-point count, which docs/04_CONTRACT.md states as a specific number (132, checked by tests/test_contract.py's K13 across at least 6 locations in that doc) -- a file I may not edit. (4) Even if I added such a function, nothing in spine/compose.py (which I also may not edit) would call it, so it would be an unread, unreachable public function -- precisely the 'declared but not built'/'armed-but-inert' shape this whole project exists to eliminate, i.e. adding it unilaterally would manufacture a new instance of the defect class this audit is hunting rather than close one. This is a contract-shape decision (should CKPT gain a package-wide DID-IT-FIRE surface at all, and if so what does it return and who reads it) that a body-writer filling in an already-frozen signature should not make unilaterally. Left save_period's body unchanged.
